transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is I’ve been forgetting things I really shouldn’t be forgetting. Not all the time, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but enough that it’s causing problems. Like I’ll miss a heart follow-up appointment, or forget to call the clinic back, or I’ll go to do a repair and realize I didn’t bring the right tools. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I figured I should probably talk to somebody about it.
Did these memory problems come on suddenly, or did they build up gradually over time?

I’m not totally sure, to be honest. I wouldn’t say it was like one day everything changed or anything sudden like that. It’s more that I started noticing it here and there, and then it became enough that I thought, “Okay, maybe I should ask someone.” Does that answer what you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I get frustrated with myself about the forgetting, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed. At least not in a way I’ve really noticed. Is that what you mean?
Have you been feeling unusually anxious or worried lately?

Not unusually, no. I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess, especially when I’ve messed something up, but I wouldn’t say I’m anxious all the time or anything like that. At least I haven’t noticed it that way. Is that helpful?
Did these memory problems start after a medical illness or procedure?
I don’t think so. I can’t really tie it to any illness or procedure, at least not that I remember. It just seemed to be something I noticed over time. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Did your memory problems begin after a very stressful or traumatic event?

Not that I can think of, no. I mean, nothing really stands out to me as a big traumatic thing that started it. It’s more like I just began noticing the forgetfulness along the way. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, every now and then I might pause for a word like anybody does, but I haven’t noticed it being a real problem when I’m talking. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been having trouble keeping track of your bills or money?

Not so much bills or money, no… at least I don’t think that’s the main thing. It’s more that I’ve been forgetting things I really shouldn’t, like follow-up appointments for my heart, or calling the clinic back, or I’ll show up to fix something and realize I brought the wrong tools. That’s more what’s been worrying me, if that makes sense.
Have these memory problems caused trouble for you at work?

Well, I’m not working a regular job anymore, so not in that sense. But I do help with a repair group at the senior center, and… I guess it has caused some trouble there. They can’t really count on me the way they used to, which I don’t like admitting.

And my doctor’s office has had to call after me about missed heart follow-ups. So yes, I suppose it has caused problems, just not at a paid job. Does that answer it okay?
Have you been forgetting to take your medications?

I… I don’t think that’s the main thing, no. I mean, I’m pretty careful about pills, or I try to be. What’s really been happening is more forgetting the other important things—like the heart follow-up appointments, or not calling the clinic back when I’m supposed to. And with the repair group, I’ll show up and realize I didn’t bring the right tools. That’s the kind of forgetfulness that’s been getting me into trouble.
Have you gotten lost in places that should be familiar to you?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, not in places I know well. I might take a wrong turn now and then like anybody, but I haven’t been truly lost somewhere familiar, at least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been forgetting recent conversations or things that happened earlier in the day?

A little, maybe… I wouldn’t say I’m forgetting whole conversations all the time. It’s more that I’ll forget things I really should’ve followed through on, like a heart follow-up appointment or calling the clinic back. Or I’ll go to help with a repair and realize I didn’t bring the right tools.

So… yes, there’s some recent forgetfulness, but it’s mostly showing up in those day-to-day responsibilities. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you had times when you couldn’t remember important personal information about yourself, like parts of your life history?

No… I don’t think so. Nothing like forgetting who I am or big parts of my past. I might be a little fuzzy on details sometimes, but important personal information about myself—no, I haven’t noticed that. Is that okay, is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been needing more help lately with day-to-day tasks like cooking, shopping, or getting around?

Well… I don’t know if I’d say I need help with cooking or getting around exactly. I’m still trying to manage most things myself.

But I guess… some people have had to kind of follow up with me more than they used to. The senior-center repair group, they can’t really count on me the same way lately, which I don’t feel great about. And my doctor’s office has had to chase me about missed heart follow-ups. So maybe, yes, in that sense I’m needing more reminders or backup than I’d like to admit. Is that what you mean?
Has anyone close to you told you they’ve noticed your memory getting worse?

A couple people have hinted at it, yeah… not in a harsh way. More like they’ll remind me, “Did you call the clinic back?” or ask if I remembered the heart follow-up.

And with the repair group, I’ve had a few times where I showed up without the right tools, so I think they’ve noticed I’m not as on top of things as I used to be. I don’t know if they’d call it my “memory getting worse,” exactly, but… it probably looks that way. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had a stroke or a head injury?
No, not that I know of. I mean, I’ve bumped my head here and there like anyone, but nothing I’d call a real head injury, and I’ve never been told I had a stroke. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you need help managing your medications?

I wouldn’t say I need someone to manage them for me, exactly… I’m trying to stay on top of it.

But the bigger problem is I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t—like the heart follow-up appointments, or calling the clinic back when I’m supposed to. It’s not so much that I can’t take care of things, it’s more that I lose track and then people have to remind me. I guess that could include medication stuff if I’m not careful. Is that the kind of help you mean?
Have you been getting confused about what day or date it is?

Not really, no. I mean… I might have to look at the calendar sometimes, but I don’t think I’m confused about the day or date in a serious way. I generally know where I am in the week. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
When someone tells you something important, do you later forget that they told you?

Yeah… sometimes. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but if someone tells me something important, especially if I don’t write it down right away, it can slip away on me.

That’s kind of what’s been happening with things like heart follow-up appointments, calling the clinic back, or even showing up with the right tools for a repair job. I’ll think I’ve got it handled, and then later I realize I missed something they told me. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you feel your memory has been getting worse over time?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s been getting worse exactly… but it’s been noticeable enough that it’s bothering me. What brings me in is I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t—like heart follow-up appointments, calling the clinic back, or even showing up to a repair job without the right tools.

I try not to make a big deal out of it, but it’s happened enough that I thought I should ask about it. Does that answer what you mean by “worse over time”?
